question.text: Mr. Karan Desai, LP in 'Konark Growth' Cat II AIF, has subscribed INR 50 crore and wants to co-invest in 'Saraswati Robotics', an investee where the AIF is investing INR 100 crore (Karan's pro-rata share via the fund = INR 10 crore). Under the 2025 CIV framework, what is the maximum co-investment Karan can make across CIV schemes in Saraswati Robotics (assuming Karan is not in an exempt category)?

answer.text: INR 10 crore (equal to his AIF share)
Unlimited, because accredited investors have no cap

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 11.9, co-investments of an investor across CIV schemes in the same investee company shall not exceed THREE TIMES the investor's contribution to the AIF's investment in that investee. Karan's AIF share = INR 10 cr, so 3x = INR 30 cr maximum. Exempt categories (DFIs, SWFs, state govt entities) can exceed this, but Karan is a non-exempt LP. **The Trap:** INR 10 cr is 1x; INR 20 cr is 2x. Unlimited applies only to exempt categories. **Cross-Exam Context:** Direct application of the 3x rule from Ch 11.9. Tested in XIX-A (distributor framing) and XIX-C (Manager-side allocation). **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Maintain a co-investment entitlement matrix per LP. When multiple LPs want to co-invest and the deal has limited allocation, allocate in proportion to each LP's 3x entitlement — this is defensible and transparent.
